decision: Retain the offline bounded service; next compare full collector workloads with physical startup, queue and delivery costs. Preserve active collectors and live execution.
falsifier: Duplicate HTTP dispatch, premature worker/subscriber slot release, fabricated acknowledgement, accepted cross-scope evidence, changed original deadlines or failed archived reproduction reopens the affected qualification.
hypothesis: Explicit local admission limits, durable original queue authority and actual client pipe receipts can bound public work while preserving deadline, orphan and lost-acknowledgement truth.
limitations: Qualification covers fabricated offline workloads with real local processes and pipes; no venue performance or financial benefit is established.
Optional planned weight is not actual API cost or proof of global shared-IP headroom.
Library service has preconnected peers, no installed daemon or dynamic listener; collector integration and study continuity remain unqualified.
Client reports are trusted same-host observations; no privileged adversary or hard real-time guarantee is claimed.
Historical ledger retention, long-duration resource behavior and realistic collector-workload comparison remain pending.
Physical timing/PIDs differ across candidate/archive runs; matching terminal contract states are not byte-identical reproduction.
